title: 〜つ〜つ
meaning: …ing and …ing (back and forth, alternately); now … now …
simpleExplanation: 〜つ〜つ joins two verbs to show actions that keep alternating: going and coming back, floating and sinking, overtaking and being overtaken. つ is a classical particle, so the pattern survives only in a handful of fixed pairs. The two verbs are usually opposites or an active/passive pair of the same verb.
whenUsed: Written and literary Japanese, sports commentary (抜きつ抜かれつ), and a few idioms used in speech (持ちつ持たれつ). You cannot freely create new pairs; learn the fixed ones. Often followed by する / の + N / だ.
formation: Vます-stem + つ + Vます-stem + つ
Opposite pairs: 行きつ戻りつ (back and forth)・浮きつ沈みつ (rising and sinking)・矯めつ眇めつ (looking closely from every angle)
Active + passive of one verb: 抜きつ抜かれつ (overtaking each other)・持ちつ持たれつ (mutual support)・押しつ押されつ (jostling)
Used as adverb (〜つ〜つする / 〜つ〜つしながら) or with の + N (抜きつ抜かれつの接戦)

rows.label: 浮きつ沈みつ
cells: bobbing up and down; ups and downs

examples.ja: 彼は店の前を行きつ戻りつしていた。
examples.reading: かれはみせのまえをいきつもどりつしていた。
examples.en: He was pacing back and forth in front of the shop.
examples.note: 行きつ戻りつ + する: the person pacing is unable to decide.

examples.ja: 両チームは抜きつ抜かれつの接戦を繰り広げた。
examples.reading: りょうチームはぬきつぬかれつのせっせんをくりひろげた。
examples.en: The two teams fought a close race, overtaking each other in turn.
examples.note: 抜きつ抜かれつ + の + N: describes a race where the lead keeps changing.

examples.ja: 世の中は持ちつ持たれつだ。
examples.reading: よのなかはもちつもたれつだ。
examples.en: The world runs on give and take.
examples.note: 持ちつ持たれつ is a proverb-like idiom: society runs on mutual help.

examples.ja: 小舟は波に浮きつ沈みつしながら、ゆっくりと岸に近づいた。
examples.reading: こぶねはなみにうきつしずみつしながら、ゆっくりときしにちかづいた。
examples.en: Bobbing up and down on the waves, the little boat slowly approached the shore.
examples.note: 〜つ〜つ + しながら describes the manner of movement.

examples.ja: 彼は品物を矯めつ眇めつ眺めてから、ようやく買うことに決めた。
examples.reading: かれはしなものをためつすがめつながめてから、ようやくかうことにきめた。
examples.en: After examining the item closely from every angle, he finally decided to buy it.
examples.note: 矯めつ眇めつ is a fixed idiom for scrutinizing something.

similarGrammar.difference: Lists mixed examples ("things like X and Y"). つ〜つ describes two alternating movements, not a list.
Modern, freely combinable "doing things like X and Y". つ〜つ is limited to fixed pairs and stresses alternation.
Offers alternatives to choose from ("either X or Y"). つ〜つ is about actions that actually alternate.

commonMistakes.wrong: 彼は食べつ飲みつしていた。
commonMistakes.right: 彼は食べたり飲んだりしていた。
commonMistakes.why: つ〜つ is not productive. 食べる and 飲む are not a fixed pair; use たり〜たり for ordinary lists of actions.

commonMistakes.wrong: 抜いつ抜かれつの接戦
commonMistakes.right: 抜きつ抜かれつの接戦
commonMistakes.why: つ attaches to the ます-stem (抜き), not to the て-form stem.

commonMistakes.wrong: 持ちつ持たれつなので、私が全部払います。
commonMistakes.right: 持ちつ持たれつなので、今日は私が払います。
commonMistakes.why: 持ちつ持たれつ means mutual give and take. Paying everything, always, contradicts the idea of mutuality.

usageNotes: Learn the pairs as vocabulary: 行きつ戻りつ・浮きつ沈みつ・抜きつ抜かれつ・持ちつ持たれつ・押しつ押されつ・矯めつ眇めつ.
As a modifier it takes の: 抜きつ抜かれつのレース. As an adverb it takes する or しながら.
持ちつ持たれつ is the one pair you will hear in ordinary conversation, often as 持ちつ持たれつの関係.
jlptTips: In 文法形式の判断, if the two verbs are opposites or an active/passive pair and the sentence describes alternating movement, choose つ〜つ.
Watch the stem: it is the ます-stem (行き・浮き・抜き), which rules out options like 行っつ or 抜いつ.
In 並べ替え, the pair is often split into two chunks (抜きつ / 抜かれつ); put the active form first.
